title: Nobody can log in
summary: The internal TLS certificate used by auth‑service expired at 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z. Edge‑gateway, which calls auth‑service over a hard‑dependency HTTP/TLS link (1 s timeout), began rejecting every request with “x509: certificate has expired”. This caused a total loss of POST /v1/session and token‑refresh traffic (edge‑gateway 5xx, auth‑service request rate collapsed). The only production change in the window was an unrelated edge‑gateway keep‑alive config tweak at 05:52 Z; it did not cause the failure. No deploy, secret rotation, or infra work touched the certificate. A previous incident (pir:2025‑040) had the exact same mechanism.

hypothesis.mechanism: The internal TLS certificate presented by auth‑service expired at 06:00 UTC. Edge‑gateway validates the cert on every upstream request; handshake failures are logged as “certificate has expired” and returned as 5xx, causing all login/token‑refresh requests to fail.
predictions: Replacing the certificate and restarting auth‑service pods will immediately restore successful TLS handshakes.
Edge‑gateway error_rate will return to baseline (<0.01) within minutes of cert renewal.

hypothesis.mechanism: Increasing the upstream keep‑alive timeout caused stale connections that presented an expired certificate, leading to handshake failures.
predictions: Reverting the keep‑alive change alone would restore logins without touching the certificate.

hypothesis.mechanism: A recent (unrecorded) deploy introduced a bug that serves an expired certificate.
predictions: Rolling back the (non‑existent) deploy would fix the issue.

hypothesis.mechanism: Clock drift on auth‑service nodes made a still‑valid cert appear expired.
predictions: Correcting system time would resolve the handshake errors without cert renewal.

facts.statement: Edge‑gateway logs show TLS handshake with auth‑service failed: certificate expired (notAfter 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z) starting 06:00:09.657 Z, 1 428 occurrences.
Auth‑service logs show TLS handshake error “remote error: tls: bad certificate” starting 06:00:06.184 Z, 1 112 occurrences.
Edge‑gateway error_rate rose from baseline 0.0021 to a mean of 0.0556 and 0.1166 at the end of the window.
Auth‑service request rate dropped from ~98 req/s to ~7.8 req/s while error_rate, latency, CPU and memory stayed at baseline.
Only production change in the window: edge‑gateway config keep‑alive timeout changed 60 → 75 s at 05:52:30 Z.
Past incident pir:2025‑040 (Aug 2025) shows identical symptom: expired internal TLS cert on auth‑service caused edge‑gateway “x509: certificate has expired” and total login outage.

assumptions.statement: The `notAfter` timestamp logged by edge‑gateway reflects the true certificate expiration time.
assumptions.reason: The log line explicitly includes the certificate’s notAfter field.

assumptions.statement: Edge‑gateway treats the auth‑service TLS cert as a hard dependency (1 s timeout); any handshake failure becomes a 5xx to the client.
assumptions.reason: Dependency graph shows hard criticality and 1000 ms timeout.

assumptions.statement: No other concurrent change (secret rotation, deploy, infra) affected the certificate.
assumptions.reason: Change history shows none for auth‑service; secret‑rotation query returned empty.

assumptions.statement: The keep‑alive timeout change cannot alter certificate validity.
assumptions.reason: Timeout only affects connection reuse, not certificate fields.

assumptions.statement: No undocumented deploy to auth‑service occurred.
assumptions.reason: Change history for auth‑service shows no deploy in the window.

assumptions.statement: Clock‑skew would not produce a log line that quotes the certificate’s own `notAfter` field.
assumptions.reason: The log includes the cert’s encoded expiry, not a local clock comparison.

actions.description: Replace the expired internal TLS certificate on auth‑service (push new cert via secret‑management pipeline and restart pods).
actions.rationale: Restores TLS handshakes; immediate fix for the outage.

actions.description: Add a health‑check endpoint that performs a TLS handshake to the auth‑service internal endpoint (or validates cert expiry) so readiness fails before cert expiry.
actions.rationale: Prevents future “healthy pods but bad cert” situation.

actions.description: Enable automated certificate issuance/renewal (cert‑manager, Vault PKI, etc.) for auth‑service and set alerts ≥ 14 days before expiry.
actions.rationale: Eliminates manual expiry risk; aligns with prior postmortem recommendation.

actions.description: Audit all internal service‑to‑service TLS certs for expiration dates and automation coverage.
Post‑mortem: document the gap in cert‑lifecycle automation, update runbooks, and add a “certificate expiry” runbook step to the on‑call playbook.

open_questions: What exact certificate (CN, issuer, serial) expired? Confirm via secret store once access is restored.
Why was this certificate not covered by the automated renewal that was supposedly put in place after pir:2025‑040?
Could any client‑side (mobile/web) caching of the failed handshake prolong perceived outage after the cert is rotated?
